summary: The code matches the design. The builder declared all four of its departures, and I found no other. What I ran: Core tests 120/120 on eng/dotnet.ps1 test; WindowCases C-006, C-012 and O-016 each passed. In C-006 the hook acted at 541 ms and the scan stopped at 550 of 30,150 folders; C-012 and O-016 each exited 70 and left no report. WindowMutants -Mutant All passed: StopDisabled, StopCollapsed, NoCrashHandler (0xE0434352), NoExitRule (exit 0), HookCompileError and HookLocked each made their case fail once, for the reason the mutant plants. Fitness: 20 rules hold. rules-parity: AGREE. I also ran three probes in %TEMP% scratch copies. (1) With the hook's ProcessPath check removed, pwsh still exits 0, but the log gains 'loaded mode=close' in 5 of 5 runs. So C-006's empty-log assertion really does exercise the non-App-host shape. (2) A real FsAnalyser.App.exe holding the hook dll makes Update-Hook's build fail with MSB3027 'locked by FsAnalyser.App (pid)' and leaves the dll unchanged. So the HookLocked stand-in behaves like the real case. (3) With OnCancel mutated to throw, the exception never reaches the app's DispatcherUnhandledException. The hook's Dispatcher.Invoke(Action) captures it and logs 'refused', and the scan runs on to Finished with exit 0. A real click would exit 70. That is the one finding. It makes none of the committed cases pass wrongly, but the driver turns an app fault into something else, and the tree slice will reuse this path. No loop in the slice history: one build attempt.

findings.claim: If the app's own handler throws while the hook is acting, the hook swallows the exception instead of letting the app see it. Act runs inside `app.Dispatcher.Invoke(() => {...}, DispatcherPriority.Normal)`. That overload has async semantics: an exception from Act is captured in the operation's Task and rethrown on the hook thread, where Run's catch logs 'refused'. So an exception thrown by the app's Click handler (stop mode: RaiseEvent reaches OnCancel synchronously) or Closing handler (close mode: Close() reaches OnClosing) never reaches App.DispatcherUnhandledException, which a real press would reach. I measured it in a scratch copy with OnCancel mutated to throw. The hook log read 'acted mode=stop ...' then 'refused mode=stop reason=InvalidOperationException: review mutant: OnCancel threw'. The app scanned 30,150 of 30,150 folders, wrote a 'Finished' report and exited 0. A real click would have exited 70 with no report. CheckActed passed on that log, because it counts 'acted' lines and ignores a 'refused' after one. The printed checks then showed 'exit code ok' and 'a report was written' for a run where the hook had failed. No committed case passes wrongly: C-006 still fails, on core.status. But the driver no longer 'presses what a person would press' when a handler faults. A throwing OnClosing would fail O-016 under the hook even though the real app would pass it. The tree slice's click and expand modes are meant to reuse this path, so any case there about a handler fault would be measuring the hook, not the app.
findings.evidence: tests/window/FsaWindowHook/StartupHook.cs:109-120 (Dispatcher.Invoke(Action, DispatcherPriority) around Act) and :79-82 (Run's catch logs 'refused'); tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 CheckActed (counts only 'acted mode=<m> ' lines). Probe: scratch copy, MainWindow.xaml.cs OnCancel prefixed with `if (sender is not null) throw new InvalidOperationException(...)`, then scratch WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-006.
findings.fix: Inside the Invoke callback, put Act(mode, app, button) in its own try/catch. On an exception, log it, then re-raise it on the dispatcher the way throw mode posts its exception: `var info = ExceptionDispatchInfo.Capture(e); app.Dispatcher.BeginInvoke(DispatcherPriority.Send, new Action(info.Throw));`. The app's DispatcherUnhandledException then sees it, just as it would from a real input event. The hook's own code stays covered by Run's catch. Also make CheckActed fail when any 'refused' line appears after the 'acted' line.

obligations.evidence: Main step of Test-C006 in tests/window/WindowCases.ps1: New-LargeTree, Invoke-HookedRun 'stop', then CheckActed, exit 0, schema 1, root, core.status Cancelled and a 'Stopped: <root>.' title. My run: the hook acted at 541 ms, exit 0, stopped after 550 of 30,150 folders, PASSED.

CheckActed runs first and returns early. In my StopDisabled mutant run the scan finished before the hook could act (log: 'refused ... the app shut down first'), and C-006 failed exactly once, on 'the hook acted', not on an ending mismatch.

WindowMutants.ps1 StopDisabled edits `CancelButton.IsEnabled = true;` to false in a %TEMP% copy. My run: the hook logged 'waiting found=True enabled=False visible=True' and never acted. C-006 exited 1 with one FAIL.
WindowMutants.ps1 StopCollapsed. My run: during the scan the hook logged 'waiting found=True enabled=True visible=False' and never acted. C-006 exited 1 with one FAIL, 'the hook acted'.

No-scan step of Test-C006: the app is launched with no root. My run logged 'waiting found=True enabled=True visible=False' and then 'refused mode=stop ... within 20 s'. So the XAML-default-enabled button is hidden, and IsVisible gates it before any scan.
Test-C012 plants '{"schema":1,"stale":true}' and runs mode throw. My run: 'acted mode=throw ... ms=672', exit 70 (0x00000046), no report and no .tmp left.

WindowMutants.ps1 NoCrashHandler removes the DispatcherUnhandledException block from App.xaml.cs (the regex must match exactly once). My run: C-012 failed once, 'exit code is the app's 70 (actual -532462766 (0xE0434352))'.
Test-O016 plants a stale report and runs mode close. My run: 'acted mode=close enabled=True visible=True ms=804', exit 70, report gone, no .tmp.
WindowMutants.ps1 NoExitRule removes the `Exit += ...` handler. My run: O-016 failed once with actual 0 (0x00000000).

Invoke-WithHook sets the three variables inside try and removes them in finally with Remove-Item Env:, never blanking them. Test-C006's cleanup step throws inside the action and then asserts that all three are absent. My run: every check ok.

Test-C006's control step (a missing dll makes pwsh exit 0xE0434352) and its inert step (pwsh exits 0 and the log stays empty) both passed in my run. My probe with the ProcessPath check removed from StartupHook.Initialize: pwsh still exits 0, but the log gets 'loaded mode=close' in 5 of 5 runs. So the empty-log assertion does catch a non-inert hook.

WindowMutants.ps1 HookCompileError (CS1029) and HookLocked (MSB3021/3027) both passed in my run: exit 1, 'FAILED: the hook did not build', C-006 never started, earlier dll hash unchanged. My probe with a real FsAnalyser.App.exe holding the dll gave the same MSB3027 ('locked by: FsAnalyser.App (31124)'), build exit 1, dll unchanged. The stand-in is faithful.

Owed to validate, but measured here against the committed hook through the committed runner: NoCrashHandler exits 0xE0434352 and NoExitRule exits 0, so the hook cannot forge 70. Fitness rule 'the hook never produces the outcome under test' holds, and StartupHook.cs contains no Exit, Shutdown or ExitCode. One run each here; the design's 30-run repeat is still validate's to do. Related: m1, where the hook masks a fault rather than producing one.

Owed to validate, but measured here: the StopDisabled and StopCollapsed mutants both make C-006 fail on 'the hook acted'. The gate coincides with a running scan: the hook acted at 541-804 ms, mid-scan, in all three hooked cases, and refuses in the no-scan window. Pressable = IsEnabled && IsVisible, read and acted on in one dispatcher callback (StartupHook.cs:65, :109-120).

cases.evidence: Test-C006 main step on New-LargeTree (30,150 folders), mode stop. My run: the hook acted at 541 ms with Stop pressable; Cancelled, Stopped title, 550 of 30,150 folders.

The committed case does not shrink the tree. The shape (the hook never acts before the ending) is fed through the StopDisabled and StopCollapsed mutants: the scan runs to its end and the app shuts down ('refused ... the app shut down first'). CheckActed's early return makes C-006 fail once, on 'the hook acted', not on the ending.
WindowMutants.ps1 StopDisabled: the scratch copy's StartScan sets IsEnabled=false. The hook log shows enabled=False during the scan and no acted line; C-006 fails once.
WindowMutants.ps1 StopCollapsed: the scratch copy adds Visibility.Collapsed in StartScan. The hook log shows enabled=True visible=False during the scan; C-006 fails once.

The no-scan step of Test-C006 launches the app with no root, so the button keeps its XAML default of enabled. The step asserts 'waiting found=True enabled=True visible=False', no acted line, and one 'refused' after 20 s. It feeds the before-StartScan state and shows it is not pressable.

Test-C012: a stale report is planted, mode throw posts an InvalidOperationException through Dispatcher.BeginInvoke mid-scan, and the case asserts exit 70 with report and .tmp absent. The absence comes from the app's delete-first at startup; the crash handler's Discard never meets a file.
WindowMutants.ps1 NoCrashHandler removes the DispatcherUnhandledException block. C-012 then fails once, on 0xE0434352.
Test-O016: stale report planted, mode close calls MainWindow.Close() while Stop is pressable (the 'acted mode=close' line). Exit 70 and no report.
WindowMutants.ps1 NoExitRule removes the Exit handler. O-016 then fails once with exit 0.
Test-C006's cleanup step: Invoke-WithHook with an action that throws after all three variables are set, then a check that each is absent. Remove-Item Env: runs in finally.

Test-C006's inert step: pwsh -NoProfile -Command 'exit 0' with the real hook and FSA_HOOK_MODE=close, after a control that shows this pwsh loads startup hooks. My probe shows the step fails when the host check is removed, because the log gains a 'loaded' line.

WindowMutants.ps1 HookCompileError (#error in a scratch copy) and HookLocked (dll held with FileShare.Read) both stop at Update-Hook with exit 1 and the build error. My probe confirms a real running FsAnalyser.App.exe holding the dll produces the same MSB3027.
No test sets an unknown FSA_HOOK_MODE. The design marked this immaterial; the branch is StartupHook.Run :72-76. Nothing to file.
No test uses a relative path or one containing ';'. The design marked this immaterial. $HookDll is built from $PSScriptRoot, so it is absolute. Nothing to file.

drift: No new departures: the four the builder listed (the committed WindowMutants.ps1 runner, SetErrorMode dropped, three extra Test-C006 steps, Start-App/Wait-App wiring with $HookDll as a script constant) are all it has, and each is visible in the tree as described.

The design's coherence_check asked the build to confirm that fitness rules 2 and 3 (scoped to tests/window/FsaWindowHook/**) now match real files. The builder grepped that the patterns match nothing; it did not show that the scopes cover StartupHook.cs. Fitness reports all 20 rules holding, but that does not prove the '**/*.cs' scope reaches a file at the folder's top level. SL-031's plant harness is the tool for that.

The three SL-033 rules sit below the '# settled by SL-' marker in .taad/fitness.yaml, so they have no ArchitectureRulesTests twin. They are enforced only by the engine's Fitness check, never by `dotnet test`. This follows the SL-031 convention and is not a defect.
